title: USM Pn1 peanut (NSIC Pn 16): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: USM Pn1 peanut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: USM Pn1 peanut is a peanut variety for Mindanao. About 88 days to harvest, 2.1 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: USM Pn1 is a registered peanut variety, also sold or known as NSIC Pn 16 or USM peanut. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2011 as NSIC 2011 Pn 16. University of Southern Mindanao bred it. It takes about 88 days from sowing to harvest, with 2.11 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Pn 16 or USM peanut, this is the same peanut. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [peanut variety finder](/crop-varieties/peanut), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

**Recommended for:** Mindanao, in both the wet and the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

USM Pn1 peanut takes about 88 days from sowing to harvest. That is 12.8 days faster than the average of the 26 peanut varieties with a day count, 101.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 2.11 t/ha beats the average of its group, 1.85. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 88 to 89 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit peanut fields most often: [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 57.1 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 2.13 t/ha dry season, 2.09 t/ha wet season.
**Fruit:** About 56 to 57 g per 100 seeds, about 75 percent shelling.
Moderately resistant to rust and Cercospora leaf spot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: mindanao's regional peanut for both seasons, yielding above 2 t/ha in both seasons in registry trials. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant USM Pn1 peanut

The registry recommends it for Mindanao in both the wet and the dry season. Mani needs loose, well drained soil to fill its pods. Pick a variety by seed size for your buyer, and one rated against rust and leaf spot for the wet season.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Pn 16 the same as USM Pn1?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Pn 16 is another name for USM Pn1, registered as NSIC 2011 Pn 16. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 88 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 2.11 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
The registry recommends it for Mindanao in both the wet and the dry season. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of USM Pn1?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
